name: Isle of the Dead (Port Arthur)
reason: Wikivoyage and Discover Tasmania name it; a distinct draw but reachable only on a paid escorted tour.
objection: Entry is only on a guided boat tour from the Port Arthur site, which a visitor may not book; overlaps the Port Arthur experience.

name: Point Puer Boys' Prison
reason: One source; seasonal escorted tour only, part of the Port Arthur historic site experience (rule 3).
objection: Genuine convict site, but not freely visitable.

name: Port Arthur Ghost Tour
reason: Operator-run evening tour; the place is the Port Arthur site (operator, not a spot).
objection: An evening ghost tour is a real, popular draw, but it is a product of the historic site.

name: Tasman Island
reason: Tasman Island is the place (Tasman NP's dolerite cliffs; Wikivoyage, Discover Tasmania) but it cannot be landed and is seen on a cruise or from Cape Hauy.
objection: Seen only from the water or from distant lookouts, so a visitor cannot do half an hour there themselves; the cruise is the operator's product.

name: Tasmanian Devil Unzoo
reason: Wildlife park at Taranna named by Wikivoyage and Discover Tasmania; hours of animal viewing, a venue not an operator.
objection: Paid private attraction, similar to a zoo; ordinary wildlife parks may be thought commercial.

name: Officers Quarters Museum
reason: Small museum at the Dog Line (Eaglehawk Neck Historic Site) named in Wikivoyage's See.
objection: One source, short visit, small museum; may be folded into the Dog Line story only.

name: Tasman Arch
reason: Classic sea arch on the Tasman NP coast, two counted sources, short walk from car park.
objection: Part of the Eaglehawk Neck cluster of short stops; a 20-30 minute visit.

name: Devils Kitchen
reason: Sea-carved chasm with lookout named by Wikivoyage and Parks Tasmania.
objection: Roadside lookout with a short visit; sits beside Tasman Arch.

name: Tasman Blowhole
reason: Tasman Blowhole named by Wikivoyage and Parks Tasmania, easy roadside stop.
objection: Near-duplicate type of Maingon Blowhole and Fossil Bay; dependent on swell.

name: Fossil Bay Lookout
reason: One source; lookout beside the Tasman Blowhole, part of that spot (rule 3).
objection: A named lookout, but a ten-minute extension of a listed stop.

name: Pirates Bay Lookout
reason: Wikivoyage names the easy viewpoint over Pirates Bay and the Tessellated Pavement on the Arthur Highway.
objection: A roadside lookout with one source and a ten-minute stay; Tessellated Pavement is the real draw there.

name: Martin Cash's Lookout
reason: Wikivoyage lists a lookout with peninsula views, reached by a long road.
objection: One source, a long winding road for a view; rarely visited.

name: Remarkable Cave
reason: Three counted sources (Wikivoyage, Parks Tasmania, Discover Tasmania); iconic cave shaped like Tasmania.
objection: Needs a 15 min walk from Maingon Bay Lookout; part of the same walk as Maingon Blowhole.

name: Maingon Bay Lookout
reason: One source; trailhead and lookout for Remarkable Cave and the blowhole, part of larger walk (rule 3).
objection: Lookout over the bay might be a fine stop on its own.

name: Maingon Blowhole
reason: Wikivoyage lists it as a one-hour return walk to a blowhole.
objection: One source; steep slippery track; two other blowholes are listed in the same area, a near-duplicate.

name: Cape Hauy
reason: Parks Tasmania features Cape Hauy's dolerite spires and lookout; a famous Three Capes walk and a major draw.
objection: A hike of several hours, only one counted source in the list (but obvious draw).

name: Three Capes Track
reason: Parks Tasmania and Discover Tasmania promote this multi-day track; the benchmark rule includes DOC-promoted multi-day walks (Hump Ridge Track).
objection: Guided and bookable by pass only, overlapping Cape Hauy / Cape Pillar spots; an operator element.

name: Fortescue Bay
reason: Parks Tasmania names the sheltered beach; second-tier beach worth a stop and snorkel.
objection: One source; campground at the end of a long road.

name: Dunalley
reason: Wikivoyage calls Dunalley the gateway to the Tasman Peninsula; a small town with a bakery and a hotel.
objection: A pass-through village with no sight of its own; Dunalley Bay Distillery and Bangor are shops.

name: Sorell Community Market
reason: Monthly (second Sunday) market: rule 4.
objection: Wikivoyage lists it, but it is an occasional event.

name: Sorell Fruit Farm
reason: Seasonal fruit-picking farm business, one source; ordinary farm shop (rule 2).
objection: Picking is an activity, but this is a plain commercial farm.

name: Sorell Churches
reason: Wikivoyage lists them as architecture seen from outside; churches fail rule 2.
objection: Three heritage churches could be a walking-route stop.

name: Primrose Sands
reason: Wikivoyage names it among the best small beaches of the Southern Beaches.
objection: One source, a shack beach village with no distinct sight.

name: Dodges Ferry
reason: Wikivoyage names a beach at the regional centre of the Southern Beaches.
objection: One source; a suburb-like holiday town; other beach towns are near-duplicates.

name: Carlton
reason: One source; a small riverside village with no visitor draw named beyond 'historic'.
objection: Wikivoyage says historic village.

name: Binalong Bay
reason: Discover Tasmania names Binalong Bay as the base and beach of the Bay of Fires; an obvious second-tier stop.
objection: One source and might be folded into Bay of Fires.

name: Swimcart Beach
reason: One source; a beach at the end of a bike trail inside the Bay of Fires listed spot (rule 3).
objection: A named white-sand beach.

name: Stumpys Bay
reason: Discover Tasmania names Stumpys Bay as the start of coastal heath walks in Mount William NP.
objection: One source; remote campground; may be part of Mount William NP.

name: Eddystone Point Lighthouse
reason: Discover Tasmania names the historic lighthouse at the north end of the Bay of Fires; photogenic landmark with a trail.
objection: One source and a short visit; remote end of the coast.

name: Ansons Bay
reason: One source; settlement and fishing spot, no sight.
objection: Gateway to Mount William NP.

name: wukalina Walk
reason: Operator-run walk (operator product, not a place).
objection: The route through Larapuna is the place covered by Bay of Fires.

name: Bay of Fires Lodge Walk
reason: Operator-run walk (operator product, not a place).
objection: Same coast already covered by Bay of Fires.

name: St Helens Mountain Bike Trails
reason: Discover Tasmania (two pages) names the trail network; St Helens is known for mountain biking.
objection: A network, not a single place; the Bay of Fires trail is a 42 km ride.

name: Beerbarrel Beach
reason: Discover Tasmania names a remote beach one hour's walk away.
objection: One source, part of St Helens Point Conservation Area.

name: Scamander
reason: Wikivoyage names the coastal town as a stop between Bicheno and St Helens.
objection: One source; a small pass-through town with no named sight.

name: Little Penguins of Bicheno
reason: Wikivoyage and Discover Tasmania both name the nightly penguin viewing; the penguin colony is the place.
objection: Only seen on an operator tour at night, seasonal; place and tour are hard to separate.

name: Bicheno Blowhole
reason: Wikivoyage and Discover Tasmania name the blowhole on a waterfront track.
objection: Dependent on swell; unfenced.

name: The Gulch
reason: Wikivoyage and Discover Tasmania name the Gulch harbour inlet with a cafe and aquarium.
objection: Harbour with a restaurant as the main feature.

name: Diamond Island
reason: Wikivoyage names the island reached on foot at low tide with a penguin sanctuary.
objection: One source, tide-dependent, near-duplicate of Bicheno waterfront walk.

name: Governor Island Marine Reserve
reason: A marine reserve for divers, an area not a place (one source).
objection: Excellent diving site, but only reachable by boat or dive operator.

name: Whalers' Lookout
reason: Wikivoyage names the short walk to a lookout above Bicheno.
objection: One source; a lookout, short stay.

name: Waubedebar's Grave
reason: A minor memorial (rule 3).
objection: A named grave of an Aboriginal leader.

name: Bicheno Motorcycle Museum
reason: A small private museum, one source; not a distinct draw (rule 3).
objection: A real, open museum with 60 bikes.

name: East Coast Natureworld
reason: Discover Tasmania (two pages) names the wildlife park with daily devil feeding.
objection: Paid wildlife park near Bicheno; commercial.

name: Lobster Shack Bicheno
reason: A restaurant (rule 2).
objection: The Gulch is the place.

name: Douglas-Apsley National Park
reason: Discover Tasmania and Wikivoyage name the park with gorges and waterholes.
objection: Some candidates are inside the park; modest visitor numbers.

name: Apsley Waterhole
reason: Discover Tasmania and Wikivoyage name the main swim spot after a short walk.
objection: Part of Douglas-Apsley NP, which is already a candidate.

name: Apsley Gorge
reason: Discover Tasmania names a 4-5 hour loop to a gorge.
objection: One source and a long loop within the national park.

name: Wineglass Bay
reason: Three counted sources; Tasmania's signature beach.
objection: The beach is part of a walk of three hours.

name: Wineglass Bay Lookout
reason: Wikivoyage names the classic lookout, a short walk from the car park; the single most visited stop in the park.
objection: Lookout belongs with Wineglass Bay for some, but the lookout and beach are separate visits.

name: Mount Amos
reason: Wikivoyage and Parks Tasmania name the summit walk.
objection: A medium-hard walk with a view of Wineglass Bay, overlapping the lookout.

name: Cape Tourville Lighthouse
reason: Wikivoyage and Parks Tasmania name the lighthouse and boardwalk.
objection: A short stop.

name: Friendly Beaches
reason: Wikivoyage and Parks Tasmania name the long beaches.
objection: Reached by gravel roads.

name: Sleepy Bay
reason: Wikivoyage names the short walk to the snorkel bay.
objection: One source, close to Cape Tourville.

name: Little Gravelly Beach
reason: One source; a short walk to a small beach within the park, minor.
objection: A park walk under two hours.

name: Hazards Beach
reason: Wikivoyage names the beach as part of the 4 to 8 hour Wineglass circuit.
objection: One source, part of a larger circuit.

name: Saltwater Lagoon
reason: One source; lagoon on the Friendly Beaches, part of that spot (rule 3).
objection: A short walk lagoon.

name: Freycinet Experience Walk
reason: Operator product (four-day lodge walk).
objection: The peninsula is the place.

name: Freycinet Marine Farm
reason: Wikivoyage and Discover Tasmania name the oyster farm outlet.
objection: A farm gate shop with seating; mainly a venue to buy oysters.

name: Melshell Oysters
reason: Two Discover Tasmania pages name the oyster tasting venue.
objection: Mainly a food venue.

name: Sail Freycinet
reason: Cruise operator (operator, not a place).
objection: Sailing around Freycinet is covered by the park.

name: Oyster Bay Tours
reason: Tour operator.
objection: Oyster tours are the same food places.

name: Spring Beach
reason: Two Discover Tasmania pages name this swimming beach with a clifftop walk.
objection: A local beach, similar to Shelly Beach.

name: East Coast Heritage Museum
reason: Wikivoyage names the local museum in Swansea open daily.
objection: One source; a small community museum.

name: Morris General Store
reason: A shop (rule 2).
objection: Historic building.

name: Spring Vale Vineyard
reason: A winery cellar door; a plain venue (rule 2).
objection: In a convict-built stable.

name: Milton Vineyard
reason: Winery.
objection: Local wine partner.

name: Kate's Berry Farm
reason: Berry farm business.
objection: Seasonal fruit and chocolate.

name: Bangor Vineyard
reason: Winery restaurant.
objection: Dunalley's wine.

name: Dunalley Bay Distillery
reason: Distillery tasting venue.
objection: Local product.

name: McHenry Distillery
reason: Distillery tastings (two sources).
objection: Gin workshops could be a half-hour activity.

name: Fossil Cliffs
reason: Wikivoyage names the fossil cliffs and a 4.5 km circuit on Maria Island, a headline island walk.
objection: One source; a walk of up to 2.5 hours.

name: Painted Cliffs
reason: Wikivoyage and Parks Tasmania name the cliffs, the island's best-known sight.
objection: Tide dependent.

name: Maria Island Marine Reserve
reason: A marine reserve area, not a place.
objection: Snorkelling spots exist.

name: Stapleton Beach
reason: One source; part of the Orford beaches walk.
objection: A swimming beach.

name: Shelly Beach
reason: One source; part of a coastal walk to Spring Beach.
objection: A swimming beach.

name: Raspins Beach
reason: One source; a local beach.
objection: Birdwatching.

name: Orford Bird Sanctuary
reason: One source; local wildlife area with no visitor facilities named.
objection: Fairy terns are rare.

name: Paradise Probation Station
reason: Discover Tasmania names the convict ruins on a road from Orford.
objection: One source; ruins with little to see.

name: Oatlands
reason: Discover Tasmania names a historic village of about 150 Georgian buildings, a guidebook stop on the Midland Highway.
objection: One source, a pass-through village.

name: Callington Mill
reason: Discover Tasmania names the 1837 windmill and distillery.
objection: One source; a distillery tasting venue.

name: Lake Dulverton
reason: Discover Tasmania names the lake with cow sculptures and a walk.
objection: One source; local lake.

name: Oatlands Supreme Court
reason: A courthouse seen mostly from outside (rule 2).
objection: A heritage building visited on the key.

name: Ross Female Factory
reason: Wikivoyage names the site in Ross; open to the public.
objection: One source and a short visit; ruins with little standing.

name: Ross Bridge
reason: Wikivoyage names one of Australia's oldest bridges with a picnic spot.
objection: One source; a photo stop.

name: Tasmanian Wool Centre Museum
reason: Wikivoyage names the museum; open daily.
objection: One source; small museum.

name: Heritage Highway Museum
reason: Small town hall museum, one source, limited hours.
objection: Free.

name: Campbell Town Red Bridge
reason: A photo stop of a bridge.
objection: Its photo.

name: Richmond Gaol
reason: Two counted sources; Australia's oldest convict gaol, run by Parks and Wildlife.
objection: Small entry fee; short visit.

name: Old Hobart Town
reason: Two sources name the miniature model village.
objection: Small paid family attraction, not a headline draw.

name: Pooseum
reason: Two sources name the quirky museum.
objection: A quirky paid family venue; reasonable shop-like.

name: Richmond Maze
reason: Two sources name the hedge maze (Wikivoyage 'worthy of a visit').
objection: A paid family attraction.

name: Bay of Fires
reason: Coastal stretch of orange-lichen granite and white beaches; Wikivoyage/Discover Tasmania name it; swim, walk, camp (rule 1-4).
objection: Long linear coast: needs pin at a main access point (Binalong Bay), and may overlap with beach spots.

name: Bicheno
reason: Beachside town with penguin tours, the Gulch, blowhole and Wikivoyage/Discover Tasmania listings: the town itself has several visitor draws.
objection: Much of the draw is neighbouring Freycinet/Douglas-Apsley; may be better as destination.

name: Campbell Town
reason: Wikivoyage lists a local-history museum and Red Bridge park; Heritage Highway stop. Arguable 30 min stop.
objection: Mostly a highway rest stop; museum open Mon-Fri 10-3 only; the Agricultural Show is an event.

name: Campbell Town Agricultural Show
reason: Annual two-day event, fails rule 4.
objection: None.

name: Cape Pillar
reason: Named sea-cliff cape on the Three Capes Track, parks.tas.gov.au and Discover Tasmania both name it; a destination walk in its own right.
objection: Part of Tasman National Park / Three Capes Track if those are listed; a 4-day-walk section.

name: Cape Raoul
reason: Popular day walk to dolerite sea cliffs, named by parks agency and Discover Tasmania.
objection: Inside Tasman National Park if the park is itself a spot (near-duplicate risk).

name: Coal Mines Historic Site
reason: World Heritage convict ruins, free access, Wikivoyage names it with its own listing (rule 1-2).
objection: Much less visited than Port Arthur; ruins with information boards only, 30-60 min.

name: Coles Bay
reason: Wikivoyage/Discover Tasmania cover it, but it is the service town at Freycinet's gate (cafes, shops, tavern); the park is the draw.
objection: Town itself is not a draw beyond services; wrapper for Freycinet National Park.

name: Darlington Probation Station
reason: UNESCO convict ruins and the hub of Maria Island, named by Wikivoyage and Parks Tasmania.
objection: Reached only by ferry; may be folded into Maria Island National Park.

name: Eaglehawk Neck
reason: Historic isthmus with Officers Quarters museum, dog-line history, and Wikivoyage/Discover Tasmania listing; also gateway to Tessellated Pavement and Blowhole.
objection: Neighbouring spots (Tessellated Pavement, Pirates Bay) cover most of the draw.

name: Freycinet National Park
reason: Flagship national park (Wineglass Bay, Hazards); three counted sources including Parks Tasmania.
objection: Likely a destination, not a spot; dup of Hazards and Wineglass Bay spots.

name: Honeymoon Bay
reason: Wikivoyage names it for snorkelling, diving and a campground; three counted sources but no coordinates and no Wikipedia article.
objection: Small bay within Freycinet, a second-tier beach; reached by drive, short visit; name is ambiguous.

name: Lewisham
reason: Small shack community; only a Wikivoyage mention of its beach as one of the small southern beaches; coordinates/views refer to Lewisham, London, so the signals are wrong.
objection: A beach named by Wikivoyage could be a second-tier stop, but the item is the settlement and no specific visitor draw.

name: Maria Island National Park
reason: Car-free island national park with convict ruins, wildlife, walks; three counted sources.
objection: Darlington is listed separately; may be a destination rather than a spot.

name: Mount William National Park
reason: Parks Tasmania national park with the Mount William summit walk, beaches and wildlife; three sources.
objection: Remote, lightly visited; may overlap with Bay of Fires.

name: Nubeena
reason: Service town and Wikivoyage lists only cafes, a tavern and a supermarket; draws are elsewhere (Coal Mines).
objection: Wikivoyage calls it the peninsula's centre and base.

name: Orford
reason: Holiday village at the Prosser River mouth and start of the Great Eastern Drive; two Discover Tasmania pages name it.
objection: No specific attraction found beyond a river walk and beach; base for Maria Island.

name: Port Arthur Historic Site
reason: World Heritage convict site, the Tasman region's main attraction, open daily, ticketed (rule 1-2).
objection: None of substance.

name: Richmond
reason: Intact Georgian village with 50+ colonial buildings, gaol, shops; Wikivoyage and Discover Tasmania; day trip from Hobart.
objection: Richmond Bridge is its headline, so near-duplicate with it.

name: Richmond Bridge
reason: Australia's oldest surviving large stone bridge (1823), named photo stop by both sources.
objection: Part of Richmond; a 15-minute photo stop and near-duplicate of the town.

name: Ross
reason: Georgian village with Ross Bridge, Female Factory site and Wool Centre museum (Wikivoyage listings), real visits of 30+ min.
objection: Ross Bridge may be a separate entry; Heritage Highway stop only.

name: Sorell
reason: Shopping hub and supermarket town; Wikivoyage's listed sights are churches seen from outside (one closed), a fruit farm and a fortnightly market.
objection: Historic town (1808) with Georgian buildings and a walking trail.

name: St Helens
reason: Largest northeast town, base for Bay of Fires, history museum and waterfront; Discover Tasmania and Wikivoyage list it.
objection: Much of the draw is Bay of Fires and fishing; the town may be a base rather than a spot.

name: Swansea
reason: Seaside village on Great Oyster Bay with a local history museum, Wikivoyage and Discover Tasmania both feature it.
objection: Small town; museum and views are modest.

name: Tasman National Park
reason: Park with sea cliffs, Three Capes Track; Parks Tasmania, Wikivoyage and Discover Tasmania name it.
objection: Cape Pillar and Cape Raoul are its own spots: park-wrapper duplicates, and a destination or standalone spot if the park clears the bar.

name: Tessellated Pavement
reason: Distinct natural rock platform, 15-30 min stop named by Wikivoyage and Discover Tasmania.
objection: Short roadside stop with tidal dependence.

name: The Hazards
reason: Pink granite range named by Wikivoyage and Parks Tasmania, but it is a viewed feature within Freycinet National Park.
objection: Part of a larger spot (Freycinet); the Wineglass Bay Lookout walk is the real activity.

name: Triabunna
reason: Ferry gateway town: Wikivoyage lists only caravan park; the draw is Maria Island, which is its own entry.
objection: Fails as vehicle/gateway; town has no draw of its own.
